bge-216-1.q: Is loving your enemies still a meaningful ideal today?
I've noticed that I can be kind to people while quietly losing respect for them. Is something wrong with me?
Isn't moral preaching at least useful for making people behave better?

bge-067-1.q: Is it a virtue to love only one person?
My partner says they love only me and no one else. Isn't that the highest kind of love?

bge-245-1.q: What do you make of Mozart and Beethoven, and why does one age better than the other?
Why do trends in music and art seem to burn out so fast, even the ones that once moved millions?
Give me your honest take on the Romantic composers.

bge-022-1.q: Are the laws of nature facts, or just interpretations?
Physicists say nature obeys laws that are the same for everyone. What is there to object to in that?
Does science actually discover truth, or does it only impose our preferences on the world?

bge-034-1.q: Can we trust our own consciousness to give us honest answers about reality?
Surely I can be certain of at least my own thoughts. Why doubt even that?
Is it healthy to be suspicious of everything, or does that just make a person cynical?

bge-044-1.q: What is a free spirit, and what is a false one?
Everyone online calls themselves a free thinker, and they all seem to want the same things. What do you make of that?
Why shouldn't the goal of a good society be to abolish suffering for everyone?

bge-232-2.q: Who has done more to diminish women, men or women themselves?
Isn't it condescending for men to tell women when to speak and when to stay silent?

bge-026-1.q: Why must a philosopher study the ordinary, average man?
I'm a bit of an introvert and find most people tiring. Should I just retreat and avoid them?
Is cynicism just a bad attitude, or can it be useful?

bge-294-1.q: Can laughter reveal a philosopher's rank?
Would the gods laugh at us?
Hobbes thought laughter was a defect to be overcome. Was he wrong?

bge-137-1.q: Can you judge a person's worth by their work as an artist or scholar?
I've met a brilliant academic who was dull in person, and a mediocre painter who was fascinating. Why does that happen?

bge-019-1.q: What is the will, and is it really as simple as philosophers claim?
I know what it feels like to want something. Isn't the will the one thing we know for certain?
Do we have free will? Explain what is actually going on when I make a decision.

bge-040-1.q: Why does everything profound love a mask?
I feel like I show people a version of myself that isn't real. Is that dishonest?
Shouldn't a truly honest person show exactly who they are to their friends?
